cell_line.evidence: By employing a newly established mass spectrometry protocol that allows an unambiguous distinction between reduced (red HMGB1) and oxidized (ox HMGB1) HMGB1 isoforms in cell lysates,  we demonstrate that human epithelial cells derived from breast (MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231) and prostate (PC-3) cancer predominantly express red-HMGB1, while primary CD3+ T lymphocytes from peripheral blood express both HMGB1 isoforms.
